chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) and said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, a man is with a group, and speech flows between them, they joke and laugh.' He said: 'There is no harm as long as it is not [something specific].' So I thought he meant immorality/vulgarity.

Then he said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would be visited by a Bedouin who would bring him a gift, then say: 'In place of it, give us the price of our gift.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would laugh; and when he was saddened, he would say: 'What happened to the Bedouin? I wish he had come to us.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on joking and laughter in Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that lighthearted banter is permissible as long as it avoids *fuhsh* (vulgarity or coarse speech), a key criterion in Shia jurisprudence for social interactions. It highlights the Prophet’s (PBUH) approachable character, demonstrating that humor serves as a means of affection and connection rather than mere entertainment, thereby encouraging a balanced, joyful demeanor in the community.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Isa, from Moammar Bin Khallad who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The man happens to be with a group, and the speech flows between them, so they are joking and laughing’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem for as long as there does not happen to be . . .’. So I thought he<sup>asws</sup> meant the immoralities.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘It was so that Bedouins would come to Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> and bring gifts for him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, and they was saying, ‘Give us the price of our gifts’. So Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> would laugh; and when he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> was sad he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> asked: ‘What happened to the Bedouin? If only he would come to us<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu al-Hassan (a.s.) ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, can a man be with a people who speak and laugh at funny stories?’ The Imam said, ‘It is not an offense if there is not that.’ I (the narrator) then thought ‘ that ’ was his signal to indecent acts.

The Imam then said, ‘Arabs would come to the Messenger of Allah and bring him gifts and then say, “Pay us for our gifts.” The Messenger of Allah would laugh. When he felt sad he would say, “What happened to the Arab man? I wish he comes by.’””
